features.name: reorganize-starter-split-pages-into-per
features.title: Reorganize starter: split pages into per-section components
features.description:
## Problem

In `packages/templates/starter/`, pages currently mix multiple sections inline in a single `.astro` file. This makes pages harder to scan, harder to reuse, and harder for users to customize after scaffolding.

## Proposal

1. **Organize all pages and components properly** under `packages/templates/starter/src/`:
   - Pages in `src/pages/` stay thin — composition only.
   - Section components live alongside (e.g. `src/components/sections/` or per-page folders).
   - Atoms continue to live in `src/components/ui/` (registry-sourced).

2. **One section = one component.** Every distinct page section (hero, features, pricing, testimonials, CTA, etc.) becomes its own `.astro` file. Pages become a short list of imported sections.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Audit every page in `packages/templates/starter/src/pages/` (including `[lang]/` parallels).
- [ ] Extract each visual section into its own component file.
- [ ] Pages are composition-only — no inline section markup.
- [ ] No regression in Lighthouse scores or `pnpm scaffold:test`.

## Scope

Only `packages/templates/starter/`. Do **not** touch `apps/site/` or other templates in this issue.
acceptance: Every page under packages/templates/starter/src/pages/ (including [lang]/ parallels) imports its visual sections from section components instead of inlining their markup; pages contain composition only (layout wrapper + section imports + data preparation in frontmatter).

Each distinct visual section (landing hero, landing features grid, about body, contact form, blog index list, projects index list, 404 hero) lives in its own .astro file under packages/templates/starter/src/components/sections/ (or a sibling per-page folder) — one section per file.
Default-locale page and its [lang]/ parallel import the same section components — no duplicated inline section markup between /foo.astro and /[lang]/foo.astro.
Scoped <style> blocks for above-the-fold sections move with the section into the section component file (layered CSS strategy preserved); no raw zinc / hex literals introduced.
Per-page JSON-LD schema arrays remain assembled in the page frontmatter and passed to BaseLayout — no section component emits a standalone <script type="application/ld+json"> tag.
No new runtime dependencies added to packages/templates/starter/package.json.
pnpm typecheck, pnpm audit:invariants --change reorganize-starter-split-pages-into-per, and pnpm scaffold:test all pass.

pnpm perf:budget passes against the starter — Lighthouse mobile thresholds (Performance/Accessibility/Best Practices/SEO ≥ 95) and total-transfer budget for /, /blog, /projects, /about, /contact are not regressed.

features.name: add-e2e-testing-to-all-templates-and-app
features.title: Add e2e testing to all templates and apps
features.description:
## Problem

Templates (`packages/templates/starter`, `packages/templates/docs`) and apps (`apps/site`, `apps/docs`, `apps/playground`) currently have no e2e test coverage. `pnpm scaffold:test` validates that the CLI can scaffold + build + pass Lighthouse, but there are no behavior tests for actual user flows (navigation, locale switching, theme toggle, contact form, search, etc.).

## Proposal

Add an e2e test suite (Playwright recommended) that runs against:

**Templates** (run against `pnpm dev` of the template directly):
- [ ] `packages/templates/starter/`
- [ ] `packages/templates/docs/`

**Apps**:
- [ ] `apps/site/`
- [ ] `apps/docs/`
- [ ] `apps/playground/` (smoke only — it's CI-regenerated)

## Coverage per target

At minimum each target should verify:
- [ ] Homepage renders without console errors
- [ ] Internal navigation works (header links, footer links)
- [ ] Locale switcher swaps routes correctly (if i18n configured)
- [ ] Theme toggle cycles light/dark/system and persists
- [ ] 404 page renders
- [ ] Per-template specifics:
  - starter: contact form submission (mocked email), blog index → post navigation
  - docs: sidebar nav, search (if present), MDX page renders

##
acceptance: Playwright is installed as a workspace-root devDependency and a `pnpm test:e2e` script runs every target's suite
Each target (starter, docs templates; site, docs, playground apps) has its own Playwright project that boots its own dev or preview server

Every non-playground target verifies: homepage loads with no console errors, header + footer internal nav navigates correctly, theme toggle flips the `<html>` class and persists, 404 page renders for an unknown route
Starter target additionally covers: blog index → blog post navigation, and contact form submission with the email transport mocked (no real Resend / SMTP call)

Docs template target additionally covers: sidebar nav navigates between pages, an MDX content page renders its prose, and the search dialog opens (search-result behaviour is covered against a built site, since pagefind requires `pnpm build && pnpm preview`)
Cookie banner is visible on a fresh visit (no `cookie-consent` in localStorage) and no request is made to the configured analytics endpoint until the user clicks accept

When `siteConfig.locales` has more than one locale, the LocaleSwitcher swaps to the localized route on click; with the default single-locale config the switcher is either absent or a no-op (matching `templates-i18n` invariants)
Playground target runs a smoke suite (homepage + 404) wired into the same `pnpm test:e2e` invocation
CI runs `pnpm test:e2e` alongside `pnpm scaffold:test`; failures block the PR
Tests are deterministic and offline: email/Resend, Plausible, and any other external endpoint are mocked or blocked at the network layer

The workflow is documented in the workspace `AGENTS.md`, each target's `AGENTS.md`, and a `tests/e2e/AGENTS.md` that explains how to add a spec without breaking the per-target Playwright project layout

features.name: restructure-starter-template-component-o
features.title: Restructure starter template component organization
features.description:
# Restructure starter template component organization

## Problem

`packages/templates/starter/src/components/` currently has four overlapping buckets:

- `ui/` — atoms mirrored from `packages/registry/base/`
- `blocks/` — one file (`not-found-state.astro`) mirrored from `packages/registry/blocks/`
- `sections/` — per-page composition pieces added by #28 (FeaturesGrid, AboutBody, BlogIndexList, ContactSection, NotFoundHero, ProjectsIndexList)
- loose `*.astro` at the root (Nav, Footer, Brand, ThemeToggle, LocaleSwitcher, CookieBanner, Analytics)

The split is unclear: `blocks/not-found-state` and `sections/not-found/NotFoundHero` duplicate the 404 concept, and "section vs block" has no consistent rule. As the template grows (services pages, case studies, more marketing surfaces), this won't scale.

This issue collapses the model to **three buckets + a single rule** that matches shadcn-style scaffolding while staying Astro-idiomatic.

## Proposed structure

```
src/components/
├── ui/                          ← atoms (registry-distributed)
├── common/                      ← shared structure + small chrome + cross-feature blocks
│   ├── Header.astro             (renamed from Nav.astr
acceptance: packages/templates/starter/src/components/ contains exactly these subdirectories — ui/, common/, blog/, projects/, about/, contact/, legal/, not-found/ — with no remaining sections/ or blocks/ folder and no loose *.astro files at the root of components/.

Every relocated component file uses PascalCase (Header.astro, Footer.astro, Brand.astro, ThemeToggle.astro, LocaleSwitcher.astro, Analytics.astro, Hero.astro, FeaturesGrid.astro, AboutBody.astro, BlogIndexList.astro, ContactSection.astro, ProjectsIndexList.astro, CookieBanner.astro, NotFoundHero.astro); files inside ui/ keep their existing kebab-case to match the registry convention.

The migration map is applied verbatim: Nav.astro → common/Header.astro; Footer/Brand/ThemeToggle/LocaleSwitcher/Analytics.astro → common/; sections/landing/FeaturesGrid.astro → common/FeaturesGrid.astro; sections/about/AboutBody.astro → about/AboutBody.astro; sections/blog/BlogIndexList.astro → blog/BlogIndexList.astro; sections/contact/ContactSection.astro → contact/ContactSection.astro; sections/projects/ProjectsIndexList.astro → projects/ProjectsIndexList.astro; sections/not-found/NotFoundHero.astro → not-found/NotFoundHero.astro; CookieBanner.astro → legal/CookieBanner.astro; sections/ and blocks/ directories are deleted; blocks/not-found-state.astro is merged into not-found/NotFoundHero.astro (no duplicate 404 surface remains).
packages/registry/blocks/ and the not-found-state registry:block entry are removed from packages/registry/registry.json; only registry:ui and registry:lib items remain.

Every starter page (default and [lang]/ parallels) follows the thin page contract: frontmatter (layout choice + i18n + schemas + data prep) plus a layout wrapper containing one or more <Composition /> imports — no inline section markup or scoped <style> block in any src/pages/*.astro.

Mirrored renames are applied to apps/site/src/components/, apps/docs/src/components/, apps/playground/src/components/, and packages/templates/docs/src/components/ for the components that exist in each tree; every import path in pages, layouts, and component bodies that referenced an old location is updated.

BaseLayout.astro (in every touched tree) imports Header from common/Header.astro (replacing Nav), Footer/CookieBanner/Analytics from their new homes; SEO/JsonLd imports continue to resolve to the same paths in src/components/seo/ or have been relocated together.

pnpm format:check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm audit:invariants --change restructure-starter-template-component-o, and pnpm scaffold:test all pass — in particular consent-gated-analytics, jsonld-graph, i18n-parallels, internal-links-localized, and tokens-only --layered remain green after the rename + relocation.

pnpm perf:budget against the starter is not regressed: Lighthouse mobile Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO ≥ 95 on /, /blog, /projects, /about, /contact; LCP/INP/CLS/TBT/total-transfer budgets in templates-perf hold.

A changeset under .changeset/ documents the restructure as a breaking change for end users who scaffolded an earlier version of the starter — listing the old → new component paths and noting that the registry:block tier is temporarily removed.

features.name: migrate-starter-template-to-tailwind-css
features.title: Migrate starter template to Tailwind CSS
features.description:
## Goal

Migrate the `starter` template (`packages/templates/starter/`) to use Tailwind CSS as the primary styling mechanism, replacing scoped `<style>` blocks where appropriate.

## Context

Per `AGENTS.md`, the current layered CSS strategy is:

- Above-the-fold components use scoped `<style>` blocks.
- Below-the-fold uses Tailwind v4.
- Beasties extracts critical CSS at build time.

This split adds cognitive overhead and creates two ways to express the same thing. Tailwind v4's compiler is fast enough that the original motivation (keep the critical inline CSS tiny) is worth re-evaluating against the cost of maintaining two styling layers.

## Scope

- All `src/components/**/*.astro` in the starter template.
- All `src/layouts/**/*.astro` in the starter template.
- All `src/pages/**/*.astro` in the starter template.
- Mirror the same changes into `apps/site/` (manual mirror per the architecture rules).
- Refresh the CLI template cache at `packages/astro-ignite/templates/starter/`.
- Regenerate `apps/playground/` via `pnpm scaffold:test`.

## Constraints

- **Design tokens stay tokens.** Components must continue to reference `--color-bg`, `--color-fg`, `--color-primary`, `--color-b
acceptance: Every .astro file under packages/templates/starter/src/{components,layouts,pages} renders its static styling through Tailwind v4 utility classes; no scoped <style> block remains except when it implements keyframe animations, view transitions, or runtime-dynamic CSS that Tailwind cannot express, and any such exception carries a one-line comment explaining the reason.

All color/typography/radius/shadow values used by components resolve through the design tokens declared in packages/templates/starter/src/styles/global.css (e.g. via Tailwind's arbitrary-value syntax bg-[var(--color-bg)] or token-derived utilities); raw zinc-* scale usage and hex literals remain forbidden outside global.css and `pnpm audit:invariants --change migrate-starter-template-to-tailwind-css` passes the tokens-only check on the starter tree.

Tri-state dark mode keeps working end-to-end: toggling .light on <html> still flips every component's surface/foreground/border via the same --color-* tokens with no need to rebuild Tailwind output and the existing Playwright theme-toggle spec is green.

The templates-css-tokens 'Layered CSS strategy' requirement is replaced by a 'Tailwind-first styling' requirement in this change's spec delta, and the corresponding scripts/audit/tokens-only.mjs --layered heuristic is removed or inverted so that the starter no longer fails the audit by omitting <style> blocks in Hero.astro / Header.astro.

Beasties is either removed from the starter's astro.config.mjs and package.json (with the templates-perf 'Beasties extracts critical CSS at build time' requirement deleted in the spec delta and its audit row dropped) OR explicitly retained with a written justification in design.md documenting that the inline-critical step still measurably improves LCP.

Lighthouse budget for the starter holds: pnpm perf:budget reports Performance/Accessibility/Best Practices/SEO ≥ 95 on /, /blog, /projects, /about, /contact (mobile, simulated 4G) and LCP / INP / CLS / TBT / total-transfer thresholds in templates-perf are met — both before and after the migration.

apps/site mirrors the new styling approach: every .astro file under apps/site/src/ that had a scoped <style> block before the migration uses the same Tailwind-utility pattern as its starter counterpart, and pnpm build --filter @astro-ignite/site is green.

The CLI template cache at packages/astro-ignite/templates/starter/ is refreshed (the prepack copy step run as part of the change, or the directory regenerated by hand) so its tree matches packages/templates/starter/ byte-for-byte except for the documented intentional differences captured in packages/astro-ignite/scripts/copy-templates.mjs.

Starter and root AGENTS.md files plus packages/templates/starter/CLAUDE.md are updated so the documented styling strategy is single-layer Tailwind referencing design tokens, with no remaining language claiming above-the-fold uses scoped <style> blocks.

packages/templates/starter/package.json gains no new runtime dependency; if Beasties is removed, the integration dep is also dropped from devDependencies / astro integrations and a changeset documents the change for end users.

features.title: Docs: add 404 page with i18n + locale parallels
features.description:
# Docs: add 404 page with i18n + locale parallels

## Problem

`packages/templates/docs/src/pages/` has no `404.astro`. When a user hits an unknown URL on a docs site scaffolded from this template, Astro serves a default unstyled white page — no branding, no nav, no translated message, no "back to docs" link.

The starter template ships a real 404 (`pages/404.astro` + `[lang]/404.astro` parallels + `components/not-found/NotFoundHero.astro` + i18n `errors.404` keys). The docs template should match.

## Proposed approach

Mirror the starter's pattern, scoped to a docs site:

```
packages/templates/docs/src/
├── pages/
│   ├── 404.astro                    ← new
│   └── [lang]/404.astro             ← new (parallel routes, one per non-default locale)
├── components/
│   └── not-found/
│       └── NotFoundHero.astro       ← new (docs-flavored, no marketing CTA)

# Docs: match starter perf + sitemap config

## Problem

`packages/templates/docs/astro.config.mjs` is missing two production-grade defaults that the starter template ships:

1. **No `inlineStylesheets: 'always'`** — the starter inlines all CSS into the HTML to eliminate render-blocking CSS requests on first paint. From the starter config:
   > "The largest bundle is ~25 KB (blog post route, Tailwind + tokens) — that adds ~25 KB to the HTML per page, but eliminates one render-blocking request and is a clear Speed-Index / FCP win for a content-light site."
   The same argument applies to a docs site: content-light pages, CSS-heavy Tailwind, FCP-sensitive.

2. **No sitemap `serialize` / per-page priority** — the starter post-processes the sitemap to give `/` priority `1.0` and `/legal/*` priority `0.3`. Docs sitemap is flat (default `0.5`), which under-signals the landing page and over-signals legal templates.

## Proposed approach

Update `packages/templates/docs/astro.config.mjs` to match the starter's `build` and sitemap blocks, adapted for docs routes:

```js
build: {
  format: 'directory',
  inlineStylesheets: 'always',
},

// inside sitemap()
serialize(item) {
  const pathname
acceptance: packages/templates/docs/astro.config.mjs sets build.inlineStylesheets: 'always' (verbatim string literal 'always', not 'auto' or omitted).

packages/templates/docs/astro.config.mjs sitemap() integration includes a serialize(item) callback that lifts pathname === '/' to priority 1.0, demotes any url including '/legal/' to priority 0.3, and returns the item; the sitemap() call also sets default priority: 0.7 and keeps changefreq: 'weekly'.
apps/docs/astro.config.mjs mirrors the same build.inlineStylesheets, default sitemap priority/changefreq, and serialize callback byte-for-byte (modulo the existing site/adapter differences).

After pnpm --filter @astro-ignite/template-docs build, every emitted HTML page under dist/ contains an inline <style> block carrying the page CSS and no <link rel="stylesheet" href="/_astro/*.css"> for first-party bundles.

After the same build, dist/sitemap-0.xml lists <priority>1.0</priority> for the / entry, <priority>0.3</priority> for every /legal/* entry, and <priority>0.7</priority> for at least one docs guide page (e.g. /quick-start or /introduction).
No runtime dependency is added to packages/templates/docs/package.json or apps/docs/package.json.
pnpm format:check, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm audit:invariants --change docs-match-starter-perf-sitemap-config, and pnpm scaffold:test all exit 0.

pnpm perf:budget against the docs template/app meets the templates-perf Lighthouse mobile thresholds (Performance/Accessibility/Best Practices/SEO ≥ 95, LCP/INP/CLS/TBT/total-transfer inside budget) on / and one inner page and does not regress relative to the previous baseline.

features.name: wire-local-lighthouse-against-a-preview
features.title: Wire local Lighthouse against a preview server + install Chrome on the autopilot runner
features.description:
# Wire local Lighthouse against a preview server + install Chrome for Testing on the autopilot runner

## Problem

`scripts/perf/run.mjs` is a deliberate placeholder. On the autopilot's Hetzner runner the script cannot run Lighthouse because:

1. Chrome / Chromium is not on PATH (`scripts/doctor/chrome-installed.mjs` emits the same warning).
2. `npx lighthouse` cannot fetch — the npm cache at `~/.npm/_cacache/` is read-only under the systemd unit's hardening (`PrivateTmp`, `ProtectSystem`).
3. The script itself only checks for the binary and emits `not yet wired to a preview server target`; it does not actually start a preview server, run Lighthouse, parse the JSON, or compare against the budget thresholds in `scripts/perf/budget.json`.

A change ago (the migrate-starter-template-to-tailwind-css PR #39), this blocked the implementer for half an hour because the migration's design required a measured Beasties LCP A/B/C. The interim mitigation was to make `pnpm perf:budget` skip gracefully when Lighthouse is unavailable — CI workflow `Lighthouse CI (mobile)` remained the authoritative budget gate. That's a fine safety net for now, but every future change that wants a local perf measu
acceptance: scripts/doctor/install-chrome.mjs exists, is idempotent (exits 0 fast when Chrome for Testing is already installed at the pinned version), downloads + extracts Chrome for Testing from the Google manifest into the configured prefix, and writes the chrome symlink so `which chrome` resolves; after running it, `node scripts/doctor/chrome-installed.mjs` reports Chrome as present (ok severity).

autopilot/systemd/aig-runner.service is checked into the repo as the source of truth for the runner's systemd unit and declares ReadWritePaths= (or an equivalent npm-cache-writable mechanism) so `npm` / `npx` invocations under the unit write to ~/.npm/_cacache without EROFS; ProtectSystem=strict and PrivateTmp remain in effect everywhere else.

scripts/perf/run.mjs `--page <route>` boots a preview server for the appropriate template (built first if needed), waits for the configured port (poll with a 30s timeout), runs `npx lighthouse <url> --preset=mobile --output=json --output-path=stdout --quiet --chrome-flags="--headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu"`, parses the LHR JSON, compares LCP/INP/CLS/TBT/total-transfer and Performance/Accessibility/Best-Practices/SEO scores against scripts/perf/budget.json, prints per-page numbers, and exits 0 when all within budget and 1 when any out of budget.
The preview server spawned by scripts/perf/run.mjs is torn down on normal exit and on SIGINT / SIGTERM — no orphan node processes or held ports remain after the script returns.

`pnpm perf:budget` on a clean check-out without Chrome / Chrome for Testing still degrades gracefully (skip with exit 0 and a clearly-labelled 'skipped — chrome not installed; run scripts/doctor/install-chrome.mjs' finding; never fail the gate on missing-tool grounds when Chrome is absent).

The previously broken `--critical-css` flag is still accepted by scripts/perf/run.mjs (kept as a no-op-compatible flag per the templates-perf delta from #37); passing it does not error and continues to inspect Beasties output for a built target when available.

AGENTS.md documents the dual-gate model in a section titled 'Performance gates' (or equivalent) that spells out: local `pnpm perf:budget` is a fast advisory check run by the implementer / reviewer; CI workflow `Lighthouse CI (mobile)` (.github/workflows/lighthouse.yml) is the authoritative gate; both must be green before a change is opened for review.

# Lint: auto-fix Tailwind canonical class issues via eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss

## Problem

The Tailwind CSS IntelliSense extension surfaces `suggestCanonicalClasses` warnings across the templates — e.g.

```
text-[length:var(--ig-sans-size)]   →   text-(length:--ig-sans-size)
```

The hint shows up inline in the editor, but **nothing in our toolchain auto-fixes it**:

- `prettier` + `prettier-plugin-astro` don't rewrite arbitrary values.
- The current `eslint.config.js` ships `@eslint/js`, `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-astro`, `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` — no Tailwind plugin.
- The `suggestCanonicalClasses` rule lives in `@tailwindcss/language-server` and is only available as a per-editor code action.

Result: drift accumulates between the long-form arbitrary syntax (`text-[length:var(--foo)]`) and Tailwind v4's compact CSS-variable syntax (`text-(length:--foo)`), unsorted class lists, and stray whitespace inside `class=\"…\"`. We can't pre-commit / CI-gate any of that today.

## Proposed approach

Add `eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss` (the actively-maintained fork of `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss` with Tailwind v4 support) and wire three auto-fixable rules:

1. **`better-
acceptance: eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss is added to devDependencies at the repo root with a pinned version, and the lockfile is updated in the same change.

eslint.config.js registers the plugin and enables better-tailwindcss/enforce-shorthand-css-variables, better-tailwindcss/sort-classes, and better-tailwindcss/no-unnecessary-whitespace as 'error', with the plugin's entryPoint setting pointed at each template's src/styles/global.css so the rules see the project's @theme tokens.
A pnpm lint:fix script exists in the root package.json that runs eslint . --fix across the workspace, mirroring the existing recursive pnpm lint filter (apps/playground/ excluded).

No raw long-form arbitrary-CSS-variable class — text-[length:var(--…)], text-[color:var(--…)], text-[var(--…)], bg-[color:var(--…)], bg-[var(--…)], border-[color:var(--…)], border-[var(--…)], ring-[color:var(--…)], ring-[var(--…)] — remains under packages/templates/**, packages/registry/**, or apps/{site,docs}/src/** that the three rules can auto-fix; running pnpm lint exits 0 with no better-tailwindcss errors or warnings.
After the auto-fix sweep, pnpm format, pnpm format:check, pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test, and pnpm audit:invariants --change lint-auto-fix-tailwind-canonical-class-i all exit 0.

pnpm scaffold:test passes; the rendered output of the starter and docs templates is visually unchanged (the rules only rewrite class strings into shorter canonical form — no DOM, no token, and no behavior change).

packages/astro-ignite/templates/starter/ and packages/astro-ignite/templates/docs/ are refreshed via node packages/astro-ignite/scripts/copy-templates.mjs so the CLI cache mirrors the rewritten source byte-for-byte (modulo the documented intentional differences in copy-templates.mjs).
No new runtime dependency is added to any packages/templates/*/package.json or apps/*/package.json — eslint-plugin-better-tailwindcss is devDependencies-only at the root.

A changeset under .changeset/ describes the addition as a non-breaking lint hardening for downstream users who scaffolded an earlier version, with a one-line note telling them how to opt in (copy the eslint.config.js block and run pnpm lint:fix).
